scope: A serum-based 2D LC-MS assay using Parallel Reaction Monitoring is applied to quantify both calcyclin and heat shock protein 90.
Maternal serum samples were collected in the first, second, and third trimesters of pregnancy in 43 patients with preeclampsia and 46 normotensive pregnant controls.
Seven microliters of each serum sample was diluted 47 times in 0.01% RapiGest

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The primary proteomics analysis was performed on maternal serum. While the text also mentions 'whole tissue lysates' from placentas for a separate PRM measurement, the core study and the PRIDE dataset (PXD009025) focus on the serum-based assay.

primary_biological_variables.matched_definition: Comparison between diseased and healthy or unaffected controls.
evidence: Maternal serum levels of calcyclin and heat shock protein 90 are compared throughout pregnancy from the first trimester till term among women with preeclampsia (n = 43) and age‐matched normotensive pregnant controls (n = 46).

replicate_hints: three technical (three PRM measurements of an identical sample (quality control) throughout the assay run) and three methodological (three independently prepared replicates of an SCX‐fractionated serum sample) replicates were measured
evidence: Maternal serum levels of calcyclin and heat shock protein 90 are compared throughout pregnancy from the first trimester till term among women with preeclampsia (n = 43) and age‐matched normotensive pregnant controls (n = 46).
Sixty‐three percent of the samples were collected in the first trimester (<14 weeks), 17 percent in the second trimester (14–27 weeks) and 20 percent in the third trimester (≥28 weeks) of pregnancy.
Serum levels of calcyclin are significantly lower in patients with preeclampsia in the second trimester of pregnancy as compared to controls (p < 0.05).
Serum levels of heat shock protein 90 are significantly higher in patients with preeclampsia in the third trimester as compared to controls (p < 0.001).
